source_text: ἀγαλλιάσεως παρὰ τοὺς μετόχους σου.» Θυΐσκη δὲ αὖ, σχῆμά τε καὶ εἶδος θυμιατηρίου, θυΐας ἐν ἴσῳ πεποιημένου, ἐπίμεστον δὲ καὶ αὐτὸ θυμιάματος· εὐωδία γὰρ καὶ θυμιατήριον ὁ Χριστὸς, οὐκ ἔξωθεν δὲ τὸ εὐῶδες ἔχων, καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ ἡμεῖς αὐτοὶ κατὰ μέθεξιν ἀρετῆς, καὶ τοῦ κατ' εὐσέβειαν ἁγιασμοῦ τὸ ἐν τούτοις εἶναι κερδαίνοντες, ἀλλ' οἴκοθεν ὡς Θεὸς καὶ ἐν ἰδίᾳ φύσει πλουτῶν τὰ δι' ὧν θαυμάζεται, καὶ ὅλην ἐμπίπλησι τὴν οἰκουμένην τῆς ὑπερκοσμίου καὶ ὑπὲρ κτίσιν ὀσμῆς. Θεὸς γὰρ ὢν φύσει καὶ ἀληθῶς, καὶ τὴν ὀσμὴν τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐν ἰδίᾳ φύσει λαχὼν, εὖ μάλα διαγινώσκεται, ἔμπλεως οὖν ἡ θυΐσκη θυμιάματος. Ταύτῃ τοι προσάγεται μόσχος τε καὶ κριὸς, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀμνὸς, καὶ χίμαρος ἐξ αἰγῶν, τὰ πρὸς τούτοις ἔτι προσκεκομισμένα, καὶ διὰ πάντων αὐτὸς ὁ γραφόμενος· ἐν μὲν τῷ μόσχῳ, διὰ τὸ ἄγαν εὐσθενὲς, καὶ ὅτι τῶν ἐν ἡμερότητι καὶ καθαρότητι ζώων, τὸ προὔχον, ὁ μόσχος, καὶ ὡς ἐν μεγέθει σώματος, τὸ ὑπερτεροῦν· ἐν ὑπεροχῇ δὲ τῇ νοητῇ, πάντα ἐστὶ τὰ Χριστοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ προὔχων καὶ ὑπερκείμενος τῇ κατὰ πᾶν ὁτιοῦν ἀσυγκρίτῳ διαφορᾷ· ἐν δὲ τῷ κριῷ, διὰ τὸ τέλειον, καὶ μέντοι διὰ τὸ ἄκακον, ἐν τῷ ἀμνῷ· «Ἐγὼ γὰρ, φησὶν, ὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον ἀγόμενον τοῦ θύεσθαι, οὐκ ἔγνων·» ἐν δὲ τῷ χιμάρῳ, διὰ τὴν ὑπέρ γε τῶν ἡμαρτηκότων σφαγήν. Χίμαρος γὰρ ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας τὸ θῦμα, κατὰ τὸν νόμον· εἰσέδυ δὲ δι' ἡμᾶς τὸν θάνατον ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, καὶ τῶν ἀρχαίων πλημμελημάτων ἐκλελυτρώμεθα, δι' ἣν ὑπέμεινεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν σφαγήν. Ἢ οὐκ εἶναι φὴς καὶ τοῦτο ἀληθές; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς γὰρ οὔ; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἐπιτήρει δὲ ὅτι προσεκομίσθησαν μὲν οἱ μόσχοι, δέδονταί γε μὴν εἰς τὰ ἔργα τῆς σκηνῆς, ἵν' ἐν ταῖς ἀναζεύξεσιν αὐτοὶ φέροντες ἐφ' ἁμαξῶν, πόνου καὶ ἀνίας ἀπαλλάτοιεν τοὺς ἱερουργούς. Ἐπαναπαύεται γὰρ ἡ Ἐκκλησία Χριστῷ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἡμᾶς φέρει, τοῖς ὑπὲρ δύναμιν πόνοις περιπίπτειν οὐκ ἐφιεὶς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ τίμιον γένος, καὶ τὸν τῶν ἁγίων ἔργων ἐπιστήμονα λαόν. Οὕτω μὲν οὖν ἀνοιστέον ἐπὶ Χριστὸν τὰ ὠνομασμένα. Τὰ δέ γε εἰς θυσίαν σωτηρίου προσεκόμιζον οἱονεί πως αὖ ἀνθ' ἑαυτῶν οἱ ἡγούμενοι, καθιεροῦντες τρόπον τινὰ τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ, καὶ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀναφέροντες τῷ Θεῷ. Δαμάλεις δὲ ἦσαν δύο, κριοὶ πέντε, τράγοι πέντε, ἀμνάδες πέντε. Καὶ μόσχος μὲν, ὁ Χριστὸς, δαμάλεις δὲ αὖ ἡμεῖς, καὶ λόγος ὁ ἐπ' ἀμφοῖν, οὐκ ἀσύμφυλος, ἀληθὴς δὲ μᾶλλον καὶ ἐναργής· ἡγεμονικώτατον γὰρ ἀεί πως τὸ ἄρσεν ἐστὶ, καὶ ἐν τιμῇ καὶ δόξῃ τῇ παναρίστῳ παρὰ Θεῷ, καὶ μάρτυς ἡ φύσις, ὁμολογοῦσα τὸ χρῆμα. Μεῖον δὲ καὶ ὑπεστρωμένον τὸ θῆλυ, καὶ οἱονεὶ κατόπιν ἰὸν τῆς ἀρσένων ἀλκῆς τε καὶ δόξης. Ἔστι δὴ οὖν ἐν ἄρσενι μόσχῳ, καθηγητὴς μὲν ἡμῶν ὁ Χριστὸς, ὑπεζεύγμεθα δὲ ὥσπερ ἡμεῖς καὶ ἐν πολλῷ μείονι παρ' αὐτὸν ἀλκῇ τε καὶ δόξῃ, καὶ, ἀσύγκριτον τὸ μεσολαβοῦν. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ γέγονε καθ' ἡμᾶς,
pass_a_gloss: [Cont. of quotation] '…of gladness (ἀγαλλίασις) beside your partners (μέτοχοι).' And the incense-dish (θυΐσκη) again: shape (σχῆμα) and form (εἶδος) of a censer (θυμιατήριον), made equal to (ἐν ἴσῳ) a θυΐα (bowl/mortar), and itself also full of incense; for fragrance (εὐωδία) and censer is Christ, not having the fragrant from outside (ἔξωθεν), as indeed we ourselves by participation (μέθεξις) in virtue (ἀρετή) and in the sanctification (ἁγιασμός) according to godliness (εὐσέβεια) gain the being-in these things, but from home (οἴκοθεν) as God and in His own nature (ἰδία φύσις) being rich in the things through which He is marvelled at, and He fills the whole inhabited world (οἰκουμένη) with the supramundane (ὑπερκόσμιος) and above-creation (ὑπὲρ κτίσιν) odour. For being God by nature and truly (φύσει καὶ ἀληθῶς), and having obtained (λαγχάνω) in His own nature the odour of the knowledge (γνῶσις) of the Father, He is very well discerned (διαγινώσκω); full therefore is the incense-dish of incense. Therefore there is brought a calf (μόσχος) and a ram and also a lamb and a he-goat from the goats, the things brought besides these, and through all He Himself is the one written/depicted (ὁ γραφόμενος): in the calf, through the very strong (εὐσθενές), and because of the animals in tameness (ἡμερότης) and cleanness (καθαρότης) the foremost is the calf, and as in size of body the surpassing; and in intelligible pre-eminence (ὑπεροχὴ νοητή) all things are Christ's, and He the excelling and lying-above by incomparable (ἀσύγκριτος) difference in anything whatever; in the ram, through the complete/mature (τέλειον), and through the guileless (ἄκακον) in the lamb: 'For I, He says, as an innocent lamb (ἀρνίον ἄκακον) led to be sacrificed, did not know'; in the he-goat, through the slaughter (σφαγή) for those who have sinned. For a he-goat is the victim for sin according to the law; and Emmanuel entered (εἰσδύω) death for us, and we have been ransomed (ἐκλυτρόω) from the ancient offences (πλημμέλημα) through the slaughter He endured for us. Or do you say this too is not true? PALL.: How not? CYR.: Observe that the calves were brought, yet given to the works of the tent (σκηνή), that in the departures (ἀνάζευξις) they, carrying on wagons (ἅμαξα), might release the sacred-ministers (ἱερουργοί) from toil (πόνος) and distress (ἀνία). For the Church (Ἐκκλησία) rests upon (ἐπαναπαύομαι) Christ, and He carries us, not permitting the sacred and precious race (γένος) and the people knowing holy works to fall into toils beyond power (ὑπὲρ δύναμιν). Thus then the things named must be referred (ἀναφέρω) to Christ. The things for sacrifice of salvation the leaders (ἡγούμενοι) brought as it were in place of themselves (ἀνθ' ἑαυτῶν), consecrating (καθιερόω) in a manner to the holy tent and offering up into odour of fragrance to God. Heifers were two, rams five, he-goats five, ewe-lambs five. And calf is Christ, heifers again we, and the account on both not incongruous (ἀσύμφυλος), but true and clear (ἐναργής); for most leading (ἡγεμονικώτατον) is always the male (ἄρσεν), and in honour and glory the best with God, and nature (φύσις) is witness, confessing the matter. Lesser and laid-under (ὑποστρώννυμι) is the female (θῆλυ), and as it were going behind the strength (ἀλκή) and glory of males. So in the male calf Christ is our guide/leader (καθηγητής), and we are yoked-under (ὑποζεύγνυμι) and in much less strength and glory than He, and incomparable is what lies between (τὸ μεσολαβοῦν). For even if He has come to be according to us (καθ' ἡμᾶς)… [continues in §33]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …of gladness beyond your companions’ (Psalm 45:7). The incense dish, again, has the shape and form of a censer, being made like a small bowl, and it too is filled with incense. For Christ is both fragrance and censer. He does not have his fragrance from outside, as we ourselves do, who come to have it by sharing in virtue and in the holiness that belongs to godliness. He has it from within, as God, and is rich in his own nature in all for which he is wondered at, and he fills the whole world with a fragrance that is above the world and above creation. For since he is God by nature and in truth, and has in his own nature the fragrance of the knowledge of the Father (2 Corinthians 2:14), he is very clearly recognized for what he is. The incense dish, then, is full of incense. Accordingly there are brought a calf and a ram, and a lamb as well, and a male goat, the offerings brought in addition to these; and through them all he himself is portrayed. In the calf, because of its great strength, and because among the tame and clean animals the calf is foremost, and greatest in size of body; and all that is Christ’s stands in a spiritual pre-eminence, and he himself is the One who excels and stands above, by a difference beyond comparison in every respect whatever. In the ram, because of its full maturity; and in the lamb, because of its innocence: ‘For I,’ he says, ‘like an innocent lamb led to be sacrificed, did not know’ (Jeremiah 11:19). In the male goat, because of the slaughter on behalf of those who had sinned. For under the law the male goat is the sacrifice for sin; and Emmanuel went down into death for our sake, and we have been redeemed from our ancient offences through the slaughter he endured for us. Or do you say that this too is not true?
Palladius: How could it not be?

Cyril: Notice, too, that the calves were brought, but were given for the work of the tent, so that when the camp moved they might carry the loads on wagons and spare those who performed the sacred service toil and distress (Numbers 7:3–8). For the Church rests upon Christ, and he carries us. He does not let the holy and precious race, the people skilled in holy works, fall into labours beyond their strength. In this way, then, the things named must be referred to Christ. As for the animals for the sacrifice of salvation, the leaders brought them, as it were, in place of themselves, consecrating them in some way to the holy tent and offering them up to God as a fragrant aroma. There were two heifers, five rams, five he-goats and five ewe lambs. Now the calf is Christ, and the heifers are we ourselves, and the reasoning about the two is not out of keeping, but rather true and plain. For the male is always, in a way, the one most fitted to lead, and held in the highest honour and glory with God; and nature is witness to it, admitting the fact. The female is lesser and placed beneath, coming as it were behind the strength and glory of the male. So in the male calf Christ is our leader, while we, as it were, are yoked beneath him and far less than he in strength and glory, and the distance between is beyond comparison. For even if he became like us…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Psalm 45:7 = LXX Psalm 44:8 (quotation begun in §31). θυΐσκη / θυΐα: Cyril explains the incense dish as censer-shaped, 'made like a θυΐα' (a small bowl or mortar); rendered 'made like a small bowl', a doubtful sense. ὁ γραφόμενος ('the one written/depicted') rendered 'portrayed'. 'Fragrance of the knowledge' echoes 2 Corinthians 2:14 (τὴν ὀσμὴν τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοῦ). Jeremiah 11:19 matches the LXX. 'Under the law the male goat is the sacrifice for sin' is a general reference (compare Leviticus 4:23; Numbers 7:16) and is left uncited. The calves given for the work of the tent refer to Numbers 7:3–8, where the leaders' twelve oxen and six wagons go to the Levites; Cyril calls the animals μόσχοι (calves), and ἱερουργοί ('sacred ministers', the Levites) is rendered 'the ministers'. 'Beyond their strength' (ὑπὲρ δύναμιν) may echo 1 Corinthians 10:13 and 'holy and precious race' may echo 1 Peter 2:9; both too loose to cite. The passage on male and female is translated as it stands. The sentence breaks off at 'For even if He became like us', continued in §§33–34.
